pieces.title: Young Woman with a Water Pitcher
note: Morning light from a leaded window falls on a silver basin and pitcher.
One of the five Vermeers in The Met's collection.

pieces.title: Madame X (Madame Pierre Gautreau)
note: Virginie Gautreau's pale skin and black gown caused a scandal at the 1884 Salon.
Sargent later repainted the fallen shoulder strap.

pieces.title: The Dance Class
note: Dancers wait their turn while the ballet master Jules Perrot leans on his cane.
Degas returned to the ballet studio again and again.

pieces.title: The Little Fourteen-Year-Old Dancer
note: Degas modelled her in wax and dressed her in a real tutu and hair ribbon.
The bronze casts were made after his death.

pieces.title: Bridge over a Pond of Water Lilies
note: The Japanese footbridge in Monet's own garden at Giverny.
He painted the garden he designed for the rest of his life.

pieces.title: Wheat Field with Cypresses
note: Painted near the asylum at Saint-Rémy in the summer of 1889.
Van Gogh made three versions of this view.

pieces.title: Washington Crossing the Delaware
note: A huge canvas painted in Düsseldorf by a German-American artist.
It imagines the crossing of 25–26 December 1776.

pieces.title: Temple of Dendur
note: Built under the emperor Augustus in Nubia, beside the Nile.
Given to the United States in 1965 and rebuilt in its own glass-walled wing.

pieces.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte — 1884
note: Seurat built the whole scene from small dots of unmixed colour.
Parisians stroll and rest on an island in the Seine.

pieces.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
note: A new Haussmann boulevard glistening in the rain.
Umbrellas echo one another across the wide square.

pieces.title: The Bedroom
note: Van Gogh's own room in the Yellow House at Arles.
He painted three versions; this is the second.

pieces.title: At the Moulin Rouge
note: Night at the famous Montmartre cabaret, lit an eerie green.
Lautrec painted himself into the background.

pieces.title: Two Sisters (On the Terrace)
note: Two girls on a terrace above the Seine at Chatou.
Feathery brushwork and a bright red hat.

pieces.title: Stacks of Wheat (End of Summer)
note: One of Monet's series of wheat stacks near his home at Giverny.
He painted them again and again as the light and seasons changed.

pieces.title: The Child's Bath
note: Seen from above, with the flat patterns of a Japanese print.
A tender, everyday moment between a woman and a child.

pieces.title: American Gothic
note: A farmer and his daughter before a Carpenter Gothic house in Iowa.
Wood's sister and his dentist posed for the figures.

pieces.title: Mona Lisa
note: Leonardo's portrait of Lisa Gherardini, softened by sfumato haze.
Stolen in 1911 and recovered two years later.

pieces.title: Winged Victory of Samothrace
note: The goddess Nike alighting on the prow of a warship.
Found on the island of Samothrace in 1863.

pieces.title: Venus de Milo
note: Found on the island of Milos in 1820.
Her arms have never been found.

pieces.title: Liberty Leading the People
note: Delacroix's tribute to the July Revolution of 1830.
Liberty raises the tricolour over the barricade.

pieces.title: The Raft of the Medusa
note: Survivors of an 1816 shipwreck signal a ship on the horizon.
A vast canvas that shook the Salon of 1819.

pieces.title: The Coronation of Napoleon
note: Napoleon crowns Joséphine in Notre-Dame, December 1804.
One of the largest paintings in the Louvre.

pieces.title: The Lacemaker
note: Total concentration on a single thread.
One of Vermeer's smallest canvases, about 24 × 21 cm.

pieces.title: Dying Slave
note: Carved for the tomb of Pope Julius II.
It never took its place on the finished tomb.

pieces.title: Starry Night Over the Rhône
note: The gaslights of Arles shimmer on the river at night.
Painted in September 1888, months before The Starry Night.

pieces.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
note: A Sunday afternoon dance in Montmartre.
Sunlight falls in dapples through the trees.

pieces.title: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
note: Turned down by the 1863 Salon and shown at the Salon des Refusés.
Its picnic scene scandalised Paris.

pieces.title: Poppies
note: Camille and Jean Monet wander a poppy field near Argenteuil.
Shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874.

pieces.title: Arrangement in Grey and Black No. 1 (Whistler's Mother)
note: Anna McNeill Whistler sits in profile against a grey wall.
Whistler titled it as a study of colour, not a portrait.

pieces.title: L'Absinthe (In a Café)
note: The actress Ellen Andrée and the painter Marcellin Desboutin at a café table.
A lonely glass of absinthe glows in the middle.

pieces.title: The Floor Scrapers
note: Workers plane the parquet of a Paris apartment.
Turned down by the 1875 Salon for its everyday subject.

pieces.title: Polar Bear
note: Pompon smoothed away every detail except the walk.
Art deco simplicity in white stone.

pieces.title: Water Lilies: Morning
note: Part of the cycle of eight vast panels in two oval rooms.
Cool morning light on the pond at Giverny.

pieces.title: Water Lilies: Setting Sun
note: The pond glows gold and violet at dusk.
Monet offered the cycle to France just after the 1918 Armistice.

pieces.title: Water Lilies: The Two Willows
note: Two willow trunks frame the pond like curtains.
The rooms opened in 1927, a few months after Monet died.

pieces.title: Young Girls at the Piano
note: Two girls bend over a piece of music.
Renoir painted several versions of the scene.

pieces.title: Apples and Biscuits
note: Apples and biscuits arranged on a chest.
Cézanne built solid forms out of patches of colour.

pieces.title: Paul Guillaume, Novo Pilota
note: The dealer whose collection forms the heart of the Orangerie.
Novo Pilota means 'new pilot'.

pieces.title: The Wedding Party
note: A family wedding portrait, stiff and dreamlike.
The bride seems to float above the grass.

pieces.title: The Thinker
note: First conceived to sit above The Gates of Hell.
Enlarged to monumental size in 1903.

pieces.title: The Kiss
note: Paolo and Francesca, the lovers from Dante's Inferno.
Carved in white marble.

pieces.title: The Gates of Hell
note: A bronze portal crowded with figures from Dante's Inferno.
Rodin worked on it for the rest of his life.

pieces.title: The Burghers of Calais
note: Six citizens offer their lives to save their town in 1347.
Rodin wanted them close to the ground, among the people.

pieces.title: Monument to Balzac
note: Balzac wrapped in his dressing gown, head thrown back.
Rejected by the writers' society that commissioned it.

pieces.title: The Waltz
note: A couple swept up in the turn of a dance.
Claudel was Rodin's student, collaborator and rival.

pieces.title: Portrait of Père Tanguy
note: The paint dealer Julien Tanguy before a wall of Japanese prints.
Rodin bought this version for his own collection.

pieces.title: The Starry Night
note: The view from his window at the asylum in Saint-Rémy, June 1889, with an imagined village below.
MoMA acquired it in 1941.

pieces.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
note: Five figures broken into flat, angular planes.
Picasso kept it in his studio for years; it was first exhibited in 1916.

pieces.title: The Persistence of Memory
note: Soft watches melt over a branch, a ledge and a sleeping creature.
The canvas is small, about 24 × 33 cm.

pieces.title: Water Lilies
note: A triptych almost 13 metres wide from Monet's late cycle.
A fire at MoMA in 1958 destroyed an earlier Water Lilies the museum owned.

pieces.title: Campbell's Soup Cans
note: Thirty-two canvases, one for each flavour the company sold.
First shown at the Ferus Gallery in Los Angeles in 1962.

pieces.title: Christina's World
note: Christina Olson, his neighbour in Cushing, Maine, in a pink dress in a field.
She lived with a condition that left her unable to walk.

pieces.title: The Sleeping Gypsy
note: A lion sniffs at a sleeping wanderer under a full moon.
Rousseau, a toll-office clerk, taught himself to paint.

pieces.title: Broadway Boogie Woogie
note: Mondrian's grid of New York streets, set to the rhythm of jazz.
His last finished painting, made after he moved to Manhattan in 1940.

pieces.title: The Rosetta Stone
note: One decree written three times: in hieroglyphs, Demotic and ancient Greek.
It helped Jean-François Champollion decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.

pieces.title: The Lewis Chessmen
note: Chess pieces found on the Isle of Lewis in Scotland in 1831.
Some of the warders bite the tops of their shields like berserkers.

pieces.title: Sutton Hoo Helmet
note: Found in a ship burial in Suffolk in 1939.
Rebuilt from hundreds of corroded fragments.

pieces.title: Hoa Hakananai'a
note: A moai taken from Rapa Nui in 1868.
Carvings from the island's later birdman cult cover its back.

pieces.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
note: A great wave curls over three boats, with Mount Fuji small in the distance.
From his series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

pieces.title: Human-headed winged lion (lamassu)
note: A guardian spirit that flanked a doorway of Ashurnasirpal II's palace.
It has five legs, so it looks complete from the front and from the side.

pieces.title: The Gayer-Anderson Cat
note: A cat sacred to the goddess Bastet, wearing a gold nose ring and earrings.
Named after Major Robert Gayer-Anderson, who gave it to the museum.

pieces.title: Sunflowers
note: Painted in Arles in August 1888 to decorate Gauguin's room in the Yellow House.
Almost every part of it is a shade of yellow.

pieces.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
note: A convex mirror on the back wall reflects two more figures in the doorway.
Above it van Eyck wrote 'Jan van Eyck was here 1434'.

pieces.title: The Fighting Temeraire
note: A steam tug tows a famous sailing warship away to be broken up.
In 2005 it was voted Britain's favourite painting.

pieces.title: The Hay Wain
note: A horse-drawn cart crosses the River Stour in Suffolk.
It won a gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824.

pieces.title: Bathers at Asnières
note: Young men rest on the bank of the Seine, factory chimneys behind them.
The Salon turned it down; it hung at the first Salon des Indépendants in 1884.

pieces.title: The Ambassadors
note: Two French envoys stand beside a table of globes and instruments.
A stretched skull across the floor snaps into shape when seen from the side.

pieces.title: Whistlejacket
note: A life-size racehorse rearing against a plain background.
Stubbs learned horse anatomy by dissecting horses himself.

pieces.title: Venus and Mars
note: Mars sleeps while little satyrs play with his armour.
A long panel, probably made for a bedroom.

pieces.title: The Night Watch
note: Captain Frans Banninck Cocq leads his militia company out into the light.
Darkened varnish gave it the nickname; it is really a daytime scene.

pieces.title: The Milkmaid
note: A kitchen maid pours milk in a thin, steady stream.
Tiny dots of light make the bread crust glisten.

pieces.title: The Jewish Bride
note: A couple, tender and still, in glowing red and gold.
Van Gogh said he would give ten years of his life to sit before it for a fortnight.

pieces.title: The Little Street
note: A quiet street in Delft, with women at work in a doorway and a passage.
One of only two townscapes Vermeer painted.

pieces.title: Winter Landscape with Ice Skaters
note: A frozen river crowded with skaters, sledges and a tumbling couple.
Avercamp was deaf and was known as 'the Mute of Kampen'.

pieces.title: The Threatened Swan
note: A swan spreads its wings to defend its nest from a dog.
The first painting bought by the national art gallery that became the Rijksmuseum, in 1800.

pieces.title: Self-Portrait
note: Painted in Paris in short, separate dabs of colour.
He painted more than 35 self-portraits, partly because he could not afford models.

pieces.title: Flower Pyramid
note: A tower of blue-and-white earthenware with a spout for each single flower.
Made when rare tulips were a status symbol in the Dutch Republic.

pieces.title: Las Meninas
note: The Infanta Margarita and her maids of honour, with Velázquez at his easel.
The King and Queen appear only as a reflection in a mirror.

pieces.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
note: Paradise, a dreamlike garden of pleasures, and a hell full of strange machines.
Closed, the wings show the world on the third day of creation, in grey.

pieces.title: The Third of May 1808
note: Madrid civilians face a French firing squad at night.
Goya painted it six years later, after the French had been driven out.

pieces.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
note: One of the 'Black Paintings' Goya made on the walls of his own house.
They were moved onto canvas decades after his death.

pieces.title: The Descent from the Cross
note: Ten life-size figures crowd a shallow, gilded box.
Mary's swoon echoes the pose of Christ's body.

pieces.title: The Nobleman with his Hand on his Chest
note: A gentleman in black with a lace ruff and the hilt of a sword.
El Greco was born on Crete and spent his later life in Toledo.

pieces.title: The Three Graces
note: Three goddesses of charm and joy dance in a ring.
Rubens kept it until he died; Philip IV bought it from his estate.

pieces.title: The Annunciation
note: The angel Gabriel greets Mary under a blue, star-painted loggia.
On the left, Adam and Eve are led out of the Garden of Eden.

pieces.title: The Birth of Venus
note: Venus drifts ashore on a scallop shell, blown by the west wind.
Painted on canvas, unusual for so large a work in Florence then.

pieces.title: Primavera
note: Venus stands in an orange grove with the Three Graces and Flora.
Botanists have counted around 190 different flowers in the meadow.

pieces.title: Venus of Urbino
note: A reclining Venus gazes out while two maids search a chest behind her.
Manet's Olympia answered it more than 300 years later.

pieces.title: Medusa
note: Medusa's screaming head, painted on a real wooden parade shield.
Tradition says Caravaggio used his own face as the model.

pieces.title: Annunciation
note: The angel Gabriel kneels before Mary in a walled garden.
One of Leonardo's earliest works, painted in Verrocchio's workshop.

pieces.title: Doni Tondo
note: The Holy Family, painted in a round frame for a Florentine wedding.
Michelangelo's only finished panel painting to survive.

pieces.title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
note: Judith and her maid overpower the Assyrian general in his tent.
Artemisia was the first woman admitted to Florence's Academy of the Arts of Drawing.

pieces.title: The Creation of Adam
note: God reaches toward Adam across a tiny gap on the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
Michelangelo painted the ceiling standing on scaffolding, not lying on his back.

pieces.title: The Last Judgment
note: Christ judges the souls of the dead across the Sistine Chapel's altar wall.
Michelangelo began it more than twenty years after finishing the ceiling.

pieces.title: The School of Athens
note: Plato and Aristotle walk at the centre of a gathering of philosophers.
Raphael is thought to have given Plato the face of Leonardo da Vinci.

pieces.title: Laocoön and His Sons
note: The Trojan priest and his sons struggle against giant sea serpents.
Dug up in a Roman vineyard in 1506; Michelangelo came to see it unearthed.

pieces.title: Apollo Belvedere
pieces.artist: Roman copy of a Greek bronze
note: The god Apollo, caught just after loosing an arrow.
For centuries it was held up as the ideal of classical beauty.

pieces.title: Belvedere Torso
note: A powerful seated torso with no arms, legs or head.
Michelangelo admired it and studied it for his own figures.

pieces.title: Transfiguration
note: Christ rises in light above disciples trying to heal a possessed boy.
Raphael's last painting; it was placed above him as he lay in state in 1520.

pieces.title: Gallery of Maps
note: Forty painted maps of Italy line a corridor 120 metres long.
Danti, a friar and mathematician, designed them for Pope Gregory XIII.
